This is a letter to the editor citing other papers, not a primary study with index tests compared to a reference standard. No clear study design or Down's syndrome cases reported.

This study focuses on deriving ethnic-specific medians for screening markers in 943 women, but does not report Down's syndrome cases or compare index tests to a reference standard for accuracy assessment.
This study compares marker levels in IVF/ICSI vs FET pregnancies (59 FET, 144 IVF) but does not include Down's syndrome cases or assess screening accuracy against a reference standard.

While this study has 17 Down's syndrome cases and uses a case-control design, it measures markers between 16-28 weeks gestation (second trimester), not first trimester serum tests as required by the review objective.

This study examines Turner's syndrome (46 cases) and other sex chromosomal anomalies (13 cases), but does not include Down's syndrome (trisomy 21) cases. The review specifically focuses on Down's syndrome screening.
This study evaluates cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in maternal plasma, not first trimester serum biochemical markers. The review objective specifically focuses on serum markers for Down's syndrome screening.
This study uses second trimester AFP measurements (165 total cases), not first trimester serum markers. The review objective specifically focuses on first trimester serum tests.

This study includes 2113 women without Down's syndrome and uses published data for affected pregnancies. It does not directly compare index tests to a reference standard in a cohort with verified Down's syndrome cases.

This study focuses on nuchal translucency (ultrasound marker) changes, not first trimester serum biochemical markers. While it includes 44 trisomy 21 cases, the index test is ultrasound-based, not serum-based.

This study evaluates first trimester serum markers (free beta-hCG and PAPP-A) with 60 Down's syndrome cases and 813 controls. It compares assay performance and reports detection rates, meeting the inclusion criteria for first trimester serum marker accuracy assessment.

This study measures ADAM12s in first trimester (7-10 weeks) and second trimester samples from 17 Down syndrome cases (after exclusions) and 562 unaffected pregnancies. It assesses a first trimester serum marker for Down's syndrome screening with adequate case numbers.

This study focuses on second trimester quadruple test screening and the effect of maternal smoking. The review objective specifically focuses on first trimester serum markers, not second trimester tests.

This study evaluates first trimester serum markers (free beta-hCG and PAPP-A) with 11 Down's syndrome cases among 2010 pregnancies. It reports detection rates and false-positive rates for biochemical screening, meeting the inclusion criteria.
This is a Cochrane Review protocol document, not a primary study with index tests compared to a reference standard. Protocols are excluded from systematic reviews.

This study measures ADAM12 at 11-13 weeks (first trimester) in 49 trisomy 21 cases and 272 euploid pregnancies. It assesses a first trimester serum marker for Down's syndrome screening with adequate case numbers and appropriate study design.

This study focuses on second trimester screening markers as predictors of adverse pregnancy outcomes in chromosomally normal fetuses, not on first trimester serum marker accuracy for Down's syndrome detection.
This study examines marker levels in 1632 women with ovulation induction and 327 with IVF, but does not include Down's syndrome cases or assess screening accuracy against a reference standard.

This study screened 2886 pregnant women using first trimester PAPP-A and second trimester markers, detecting 11 Down's syndrome cases. It reports detection rates and false-positive rates for serum marker screening, meeting the inclusion criteria for first trimester serum tests.
